reading.body:
OptimumHQ is a software company, not a data center, and should not be counted as AI compute infrastructure.

The listing carries a data center tag and coordinates in Mesa, Arizona, but the company builds AI-powered ERP, CRM, and business automation software. Its own site gives an address in Gilbert, while the record on file gives one in Mesa. Val Vista Drive runs through both cities, so the gap may be an old office, a mapping error, or a different suite in a shared complex. Reverse geocoding at the stored coordinates returns no business name, and the same address appears against another unrelated registry row, which points to a multi-tenant building rather than a dedicated facility. No server capacity, power draw, or colocation service is published for either address.

The pattern matters because facility counts are only as good as their tags. Arizona has 56 mapped facilities with data center tags, and only 4 publish power consumption figures, totaling 512 MW. A software office swept into that set inflates the count without adding a single megawatt. Since every AI capability is downstream of compute, and compute is downstream of buildings and power, a mistagged building is a small but real error in the map of where the constraint binds.

What this record does not tell you is whether OptimumHQ runs any servers at all, or where it actually operates. It also does not establish that the other 55 Arizona entries are accurate. It covers one address, several miles from the other 8 rows in its batch, and no single shared building connects all 9.
